title: BBQ Smoker Temperature Stall Detection
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe probe=meat
| timechart span=10m avg(temp_c) as meat_temp
| streamstats current=f last(meat_temp) as prev
| eval climb=meat_temp-prev, stalled=if(climb<0.3 AND meat_temp>63 AND meat_temp<74,1,0)
description: Detects the notorious brisket stall, when the meat temperature plateaus for hours, so you know whether to wait it out or wrap.
value: The stall panics first-time smokers into ruining dinner; spotting it for what it is turns a scary plateau into a planned step.
implementation: Feed a meat-probe into `index=personal`; run during a cook and flag when the temperature climb flattens in the stall zone.
visualization: Line chart of meat temperature with the stall zone shaded.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Kitchen, Cooking & Fermentation — typical feeds: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), .
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `bbq:probe`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=bbq:probe`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Feed a meat-probe into `index=personal`; run during a cook and flag when the temperature climb flattens in the stall zone.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "bbq:probe", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **BBQ Smoker Temperature Stall Detection** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=bbq:probe`) across the full search range. `eventstats` / `streamstats` compute rolling baselines before filtering outliers; window size controls sensitivity (smaller window = noisier alerts).

**Fields this search depends on:** `climb`, `meat_temp`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe probe=meat
| timechart span=10m avg(temp_c) as meat_temp
| streamstats current=f last(meat_temp) as prev
| eval climb=meat_temp-prev, stalled=if(climb<0.3 AND meat_temp>63 AND meat_temp<74,1,0)
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table climb, meat_temp
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `climb` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(climb) AS p50 perc90(climb) AS p90 perc99(climb) AS p99 max(climb) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.15.3: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Line Chart Of Meat Temperature With The Stall Zone Shaded (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `bbq:probe` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=bbq:probe | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Everything is an outlier:** Baseline window is too short or `stdev=0` — require minimum sample count (`where count>=5`) before computing z-scores.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=10m` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `10m` buckets.
